profile.summary: The GPN paper's own check of how well its DNA language model, trained on eight Brassicales genomes, predicts held-out Arabidopsis thaliana sequence and how well its embeddings separate gene regions. It reports test perplexity on a held-out chromosome, perplexity by position class in a 1-Mb test region, and a leave-one-chromosome-out classifier of gene regions from averaged embeddings. It is useful to plant genomics researchers comparing DNA language models on A. thaliana, but only the authors' own models are scored.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things about a masked DNA language model. First, how well it predicts nucleotides it has not seen, measured as perplexity on a held-out chromosome, genome-wide and in non-repeat regions, and by position class (splice sites, start and stop codons, codon positions, intergenic and intronic) in a 1-Mb test region. Second, whether its embeddings, learned without labels, carry gene structure: a classifier trained on embeddings averaged over 100-bp windows must assign each window to a gene region class.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'Unsupervised Clustering of Genomic Regions' and 'DNA Motifs Revealed by High-Confidence Model Predictions'; Materials and Methods, 'Motif Analysis'

quotes.text: Perplexity is defined as the exponentiation of the cross-entropy loss, which is equivalent to 1 over the probability given to the correct nucleotide.

The held-out model perplexity was computed for splice acceptors, splice donors, start codons, stop codons, CDS, and intergenic and intronic positions in the 1-Mb region Chr5:3,500,000-4,500,000, after excluding repeats.

To understand how well the model has learned the structure of the genome, we averaged GPN’s contextual embeddings (512 dimensions) of nucleotides over 100 base pair (bp) windows from the reference genome and visualized them using UMAP

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: The model was trained on 8 RefSeq-annotated Brassicales reference genomes. Arabidopsis thaliana chromosome 4 was held out for validation and chromosome 5 for testing. Training windows of 512 bp were drawn with emphasis on exons, promoters and an equal amount of random windows. For the embedding task, gene annotation came from EnsemblPlants; intergenic windows fully covered by repeats form a separate Repeat class, and windows with ambiguous annotation were dropped.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Perplexity is the exponential of the cross-entropy loss; lower is better. Table S2 reports chromosome-wide and non-repeat test perplexity for three models that differ only in the loss weight on repeats. For gene regions, a scikit-learn logistic regression with inverse-frequency class weights and cross-validated L2 strength is trained on standardised window embeddings; each chromosome is predicted by a model trained on the others. The text reports per-class accuracy only for CDS (96%) and ncRNA (51%), and says k-mer frequency features do worse (SI Appendix, Figure S1).
